neutral_facts.value: The accused and the deceased were involved in a dispute over the sale of property. On the day of the incident, the accused and his father arrived at the office of a third party where the deceased and his brothers were already present. An altercation occurred between the accused and the deceased, leading to a scuffle. During the scuffle, the deceased and his brothers attempted to strangle the accused. The accused reached for his revolver, and upon seeing the gun, the deceased released him and started running. The accused then fired the shot, which hit the deceased from behind. The bullet entered the body below the right shoulder and traveled upwards without exiting. The medical evidence indicated that the shot was fired from a distant range, and there was no blackening or charring around the wound. The accused was convicted of murder, but the conviction was later overturned on the grounds that the accused acted in self-defense without premeditation.

witness_credibility.value: The court assessed the credibility of the witnesses by noting that PW-3 (Hans Raj) did not specify that the appellant shot him, and that the version of PW-30 (Tarsem Kumar) was doubted due to the bullet entry wound being on the back of the deceased, not the front. The court also found that the testimony of PW-23 (Subhash Chand Mahajan) and PW-27 (Sarover Kumar) about the scuffle was unshaken in cross-examination.

appeal_history.value: Trial court: Conviction under Sections 302 and 304 read with Section 34 of IPC. High Court: Conviction under Sections 302 and 304 read with Section 34 of IPC. Supreme Court: Conviction under Section 302 for murder of Kishan Lal is set aside, and conviction under Section 304 is maintained.

quotes.text: The appellant has also been convicted under Section 302 IPC for the murder of Kishan Lal. Hans Raj (PW-3) deposed that the appellant fired at his brother, and when PW-3 and his brothers tried to catch hold of the appellant, the appellant told his father to finish all the brothers.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the appellant shot the deceased and his brothers during a confrontation, resulting in their deaths, and that the appellant took undue advantage of the situation by using the gun even though the deceased and his brothers were unarmed.

quotes.text: It is not possible to accept the argument of the prosecution that the appellant took undue advantage of the situation and used the gun even though the deceased-Shyam Sunder and his brothers were unarmed.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the appellant acted in self-defence, as he was being strangled by the deceased and his brothers during a scuffle, and that the shooting was a result of a sudden fight in the heat of passion, not premeditation.

quotes.text: The appellant may have apprehended a danger to his life when the deceased and his brothers started strangulating him after pushing him to the floor. A mere reasonable apprehension is enough to put the right of self-defence into operation.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that a person in imminent and reasonable danger of losing their life or limb may use self-defence, even if it results in the death of the assailant, provided it is without premeditation and without taking undue advantage.

quotes.text: A person who is in imminent and reasonable danger of losing his life or limb may in exercise of self-defence inflict any harm even extending to death on his assailant either when the assault is attempted or upon being directly threatened.

sentencing_rationale.value: The final sentence was imposed because the appellant was already serving a sentence of 13 years, and the court sentenced him to the period already undergone under Section 304 of the IPC.

quotes.text: Since the appellant has already undergone a sentence of 13 Y, years as on date, he is sentenced under section 304 IPC to the period already undergone.

judicial_mitigating_factors.value: The court considered that the appellant acted in self-defence without premeditation and that the shooting occurred in a sudden fight in the heat of passion.

quotes.text: The homicide in the present case thus does not amount to murder in the view of Exception 2 to Section 300 of IPC. The Sessions Court and the High Court rightly observed that the homicide was not the result of premeditation but rather, as the evidence suggests, the shooting took place in a sudden fight in the heat of passion.
